name: Palazzo Avino
insider_take: This 12th-century palazzo perched 300 feet above the Mediterranean isn't just a hotel—it's a clifftop sanctuary where Hollywood royalty and European aristocracy have escaped for decades.
whats_special: Palazzo Avino occupies a former noble residence with hand-painted Vietri ceramics adorning every surface, while its Michelin-starred restaurant Rossellinis offers the only fine dining experience directly overlooking the Amalfi Coast's most dramatic coastline. The hotel's private beach club, accessible via a scenic funicular ride, sits on a secluded cove that was once a favorite hideaway of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis.
pro_tip: Book the Belvedere Suite for the same panoramic terrace view that inspired countless scenes in "The Talented Mr. Ripley," filmed just minutes away in nearby Positano.
dont_miss: The sunset aperitivo on the Lobster & Martini Bar terrace, where you can sip cocktails while watching the sun melt into the Tyrrhenian Sea—a view that stretches uninterrupted from Capri to the Cilento Peninsula. The hotel's cooking school also offers hands-on lessons in preparing traditional Campanian dishes using lemons from the property's own terraced groves.
pros: Stunning clifftop location with panoramic views of the Mediterranean Sea and Amalfi Coast
Michelin-starred restaurant Rossellinis offering exceptional fine dining experience
Luxurious spa and wellness facilities with traditional treatments
Elegant rooms and suites with authentic Italian design and modern amenities
Prime location in Ravello with easy access to historic attractions and cultural sites
cons: Premium pricing reflects luxury positioning and exclusive location
Limited parking availability due to historic town setting
